items.question: Why does the LFM3-Harness matter for local AI?
items.answer: An independent, MIT-licensed community project published November 1–2, 2026 — not affiliated with Liquid AI — that wires four of Liquid's LFM3 models into a supervised local agent stack: a d1-2B router, an LFM3-1.7B actor, LFM3-VL-2B for vision and LFM3-Audio-2B for voice, all pinned to CPU llama.cpp servers on 127.0.0.1. Its supervision machinery includes a 75%-floor preflight write gate, frozen SHA-256 acceptance contracts, finish claims refused until the file exists on disk, hints separated from authority, and expiring allow-once approvals. Its own benchmark run caught its router silently faking itself — the failure mode the harness exists to catch.
